subject: microbiology
title: Tumbling Motility and Listeria Identification Systems

steps.tx: **Tumbling motility** is Listeria's end over end somersaulting in broth at 20 to 25 degrees, peritrichous flagella expressed at room temperature and silenced at 37 (virulence programme switch), read in hanging drop or wet mount, with umbrella shaped growth below the surface of semisolid agar at room temperature confirming in parallel.
steps.say: Tumbles at room temperature, still at body temperature: Listeria motility is temperature theatre.

right.title: Semisolid read
points: Umbrella layer 3 to 5 mm below surface

steps.tx: **Tumbling motility** is the end over end somersault of Listeria in broth at twenty to twenty five degrees. Peritrichous flagella are expressed at room temperature and silenced at thirty seven degrees, a switch tied to the virulence programme. The pattern is read in a hanging drop or wet mount. Umbrella shaped growth below the surface of semisolid agar at room temperature confirms the same temperature dependent motility in parallel.
steps.say: Listeria tumbles end over end in broth at room temperature because peritrichous flagella are on, then grows still at body temperature when those flagella switch off. A hanging drop shows the tumble. Umbrella growth in semisolid agar at room temperature agrees.

vis.alt: A wet mount sketch shows rod shaped bacteria tumbling end over end in fluid.
vis.caption: Rods in a room temperature wet mount tumble end over end, the motility pattern of Listeria. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Temperature regulation** in Listeria links bench to virulence: PrfA regulon (internalins, listeriolysin, ActA) activates at 37 degrees while flagella turn off, an environmental to host programme switch RNA thermosensors mediate. The refrigerator organism becomes intracellular invader by thermometer. The same thermometer logic explains why motility tests incubated only at body temperature can miss the organism completely.
steps.say: Cold grows flagella, warmth grows invasion genes; temperature is Listeria's career switch.

right.title: Host mode
points: Actin based spread cell to cell

steps.tx: **Cold enrichment** (specimens held at 4 degrees with weekly subculture for weeks) was Listeria isolation's historic trick, psychrotroph outgrowing rivals in fridges, now selective chromogenic agars (ALOA showing phospholipase halos) and PCR shorten it. The principle remains examinable: exploit the trait rivals lack.
steps.say: Hold it cold and let rivals die: enrichment by refrigerator, Listeria's signature trick.

left.title: Historic method
points: Slow but specific in pre selective era

steps.tx: **Intracellular life cycle** in sequence: internalin A binds E cadherin (intestine, placenta), internalin B Met receptor (liver), phagosome escaped by listeriolysin O and phospholipases, cytosolic doubling, ActA polar actin comet propulsion into neighbour cell membrane, double membrane vacuole escaped again, antibody bypassed throughout.
steps.say: Invade, escape, ride actin, repeat: Listeria never needs to face antibody between cells.

steps.tx: **Pregnancy listeriosis** mechanics (placental trophoblast invasion, granulomatous microabscesses, fetal septicaemia granulomatosis infantiseptica, late neonatal meningitis from birth canal) dictate maternal blood cultures in febrile third trimester flu, ampicillin urgently, placenta to microbiology and histology always. Blood cultures drawn during that apparently mild maternal illness may be the only warning before delivery turns catastrophic.
steps.say: Febrile flu in late pregnancy gets blood cultures and ampicillin thinking, placenta to the laboratory.

steps.tx: **Listeria meningitis pattern** (subacute, gram positive rod hunted in mononuclear CSF, rhombencephalitis brainstem variant in healthy adults with cranial nerve signs) and empiric ampicillin age rules (neonates, over fifties, pregnancy, immunocompromise) are prescriptions this bacterium personally wrote into guidelines. Cerebrospinal fluid may show surprisingly few organisms, so negative Gram stains carry little reassurance in the right host.
steps.say: Brainstem encephalitis in a healthy adult is Listeria until proven otherwise.

left.title: CNS portraits
points: CSF gram stain positive only minority

right.title: Empiric rules
points: Add ampicillin: neonate, pregnancy, over 50, immunocompromised
Dexamethasone meningitis rules vary with Listeria suspicion

steps.tx: **Outbreak genomics** for Listeria (core genome MLST clusters linking deli, ice cream, melon and cheese cases across years, persistent factory strains) changed food investigation from culture luck to sequence led, with patient food histories reinterviewed when genomes match. Food histories therefore extend over weeks rather than days, and refrigerator contents may be cultured when a genomic match points to a product.
steps.say: Genomes remember what patients ate months ago; clusters emerge from freezers of sequences.

left.title: Investigation tools
points: Recall thresholds by match and product risk

right.title: Clinical echoes
points: Ask stored food histories in cases
Long incubation (up to 70 days) blurs recall

steps.tx: **Motility differentials** among gram positive rods close: Listeria tumbling, Erysipelothrix non motile, Bacillus peritrichous vigorous, Corynebacterium non motile, Lactobacillus non motile; temperature pattern separates Listeria from Bacillus where colony similarity tempts. A bench that fails to test motility at the cooler temperature loses this separation and may need molecular methods to recover the answer.
steps.say: Tumbling cool, Bacillus always, coryneforms never: motility sorts the rods.

right.title: Temperature clues
points: Yersinia enterocolitica motile cool not warm parallel
Cold growth itself a Listeria flag
Bench incubators set both temperatures deliberately
